brief.topic: A Fair Sample Without Keeping the Whole Stream

s01: Suppose messages arrive one at a time, and you can keep only one.
You want every message to have the same chance, even though you do not know when the stream will end.
When the second arrives, replace the stored message with probability one half.
When the third arrives, replace it with probability one third.
A smaller chance for the newcomer may seem unfair.
But an earlier message has already survived a selection.
After two messages, A and B each have probability one half.
Either stays only when the third message is not chosen: probability two thirds.
One half times two thirds is one third.
The new message also has probability one third.
With four messages, replace with probability one quarter.
Each earlier chance becomes one third times three quarters, which is one quarter.
At step n, the replacement chance is one divided by n.
The same cancellation keeps every message equally likely.
This is reservoir sampling with one stored item.
The letters here explain the possible outcomes; the algorithm keeps just one message and a counter.
It can sample a large data stream without storing the whole stream.
Equal chances come from balancing arrival with survival.

scenes.narration:
Suppose messages arrive one at a time, and you can keep only one. You want every message to have the same chance, even though you do not know when the stream will end.

Keep the first message. When the second arrives, replace the stored message with probability one half. When the third arrives, replace it with probability one third. A smaller chance for the newcomer may seem unfair.

But an earlier message has already survived a selection. After two messages, A and B each have probability one half. Either stays only when the third message is not chosen: probability two thirds. One half times two thirds is one third. The new message also has probability one third.

With four messages, replace with probability one quarter. Each earlier chance becomes one third times three quarters, which is one quarter. At step n, the replacement chance is one divided by n. The same cancellation keeps every message equally likely.

This is reservoir sampling with one stored item. The letters here explain the possible outcomes; the algorithm keeps just one message and a counter. It can sample a large data stream without storing the whole stream. Equal chances come from balancing arrival with survival.
